guide.summary: Use OAuth2 against each customer's own Forgejo instance. The instance administrator must register the app at the instance admin applications page. Forgejo's OAuth grant has no scope selection, and the token carries administrative rights, so the read-only boundary cannot be enforced by the grant. Use the repository search endpoint for visible repositories and follow pagination links until none remain. Test with your own instance first. Whether an empty query returns every visible repository is unverified.

findings.title: OAuth2 provider is documented for third-party apps
findings.detail: Forgejo supports third-party apps obtaining user consent. OAuth apps are registered instance-wide by an administrator, so each customer's instance needs its own registration.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

findings.title: OAuth token has administrative rights, not a narrow grant
findings.detail: A third-party app that obtains a user token gets administrative rights. OAuth scopes are not implemented, so the read-only use case cannot be enforced through the grant. Disclose this to customers.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

findings.title: No OAuth scope to request for the read
findings.detail: No OAuth scope identifier is documented, so no permission is requested. Scoped access tokens and personal tokens are separate from OAuth and are not used for this flow.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;

findings.title: Repository search covers visible repositories
findings.detail: The search endpoint includes private repositories the user can access by default. The owned-repositories endpoint returns only repositories the user owns, so it is not sufficient for visible repositories.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
## GET /api/v1/user/repos | List the repos that the authenticated user owns

findings.title: Pagination uses page, limit and Link headers
findings.detail: The API supports page and limit parameters. Link headers give next and last pages, and x-total-count gives the total. Maximum page size is read from the instance settings endpoint.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
The default and maximum values for the page parameter can be obtained from the https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/settings/api endpoint.

findings.title: Authorization and token exchange endpoints
findings.detail: Redirect the user to the authorize endpoint with client ID, redirect URI, response type code and state. Exchange the returned code at the token endpoint. The redirect URI must match in both requests. Use the access token as a Bearer header.

evidence.quote: https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an application in the settings. The STATE is a random string that will be
POST https://[YOUR-FORGEJO-URL]/login/oauth/access_token { "client_id" : "YOUR_CLIENT_ID" ,
The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.
HTTP basic authentication Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
